interpreter_rule: every start of the framework interpreter with -B

checks.name: documentation
checks.note: run while this record was a placeholder, so that the links to it resolve

checks.name: whitespace, every staged file
checks.reason: trailing spaces only in W1's verbatim diff record workers/W1-correction/CHANGES.diff, whose blank context lines are a single space, and in this check's own output, which quotes them; preserved as recorded

checks.name: whitespace, authored files
checks.command: git diff --cached --check -- . ':!<the verbatim diff record>' ':!<the two whitespace checks' own outputs>'

checks.name: privacy search of every staged file
checks.command: the derived private terms, the per-user temporary directory and a /var/folders pattern after the accepted contexts; the joined and squeezed string constants of every staged Python file; the application terms counted
accepted_classes: python@3.12 only inside <prefix>/Cellar/... and <prefix>/opt/... interpreter paths and their relative link target, as in MH

macOS's own system paths (/System/Volumes/...), a public wheel's recorded build path (/Users/runner), a prose mention of the temporary directory's form, one reviewer's regular expression of generic path prefixes, one control author's privacy guard of the same generic prefixes, and a table of the system's own links
one joined test name, as in MH and commit B
checks.joined_constant_reading: each hit is either a machine path's generic prefix that the text search accepts in context, or a false positive formed across adjacent constants and absent in the source ('actual' + 'expected', 'equal' + 'expected', 'canonical' + 'exactly')
checks.application_term_reading: only the project's own workflow vocabulary (Claude, ChatGPT), generic words in test IDs and prose, and one standard-library file name in the Python inventory
